correctness.rationale: For odd inputs, t=s/(uv), so the zero slice has q/2 ordered pairs and nonzero s,t must have the same positive valuation h. Divide by 2^h and translate by the integral half of s. The resulting square roots modulo 2^(k-h) must be even for h=1 and odd otherwise; each lifts 2^h times. The odd-unit squaring kernel has size four from modulus 8 onward (x²=1 forces x=±1 modulo half the modulus), giving all unit targets 1 mod 8, with the two smaller moduli checked separately. Nonzero even square counts follow by extracting the root valuation; zero roots are multiples of 2^ceil((k-h)/2). As t varies, these targets cover all of the specified parity, so the h>=2 support contributes q²/192+5/3 and the h=1 support contributes (q/4) times q/48+5/3 for even k or q/48+4/3 for odd k, plus the origin. For energy the equal-sum quadruple parametrization reduces to a product zero modulo 2^K, K=k-3, with odd variable sum and precisely one odd factor. The two even factors have K*2^(K-1) admissible pairs (directly for K=1, otherwise truncate the valuation after dividing both by 2). Including the 128 lifts gives 3(k-3)q²/2. Orthogonality gives the stated q^(-2) normalization. The verification note and uploaded checker were read, not executed.
